solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Stopping hostile takeover, how awful to be made to pay

indicators.note: one piece stops up the other, plugging the gap in its middle

parts.note: a coup is a hostile takeover of a state
ugh is an exclamation of disgust, how awful

explanation.surface: A company fends off a hostile bid, and somebody ends up footing the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: UGH sits inside COUP, 'Stopping' it like a plug.
explanation.definitionFit: To hand over money reluctantly, under pressure, is the idiom for paying when forced to.

clue.text: Take place apart from those in Teton Range

indicators.note: apart from says those inner letters are left out

parts.note: come to pass means to take place, happen

indicators.note: those in a word are its inner letters, excluding first and last

explanation.surface: Somewhere apart from the climbers in the Teton Range of Wyoming.
explanation.walkthrough: COME TO PASS minus ETO, the inner letters of Teton. 'Range' looks part of a mountain name but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Scope or extent, as in the compass of a voice: a synonym for range.

clue.text: Illicit articles, all from the EU in opposition

parts.note: un is a French article, der a German one and the an English one, all from EU languages
counter as a noun means opposition, a counteraction

explanation.surface: Illegal items from the European Union in the opposition's hands.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definite and indefinite articles in European languages: French UN, German DER, English THE (written when Britain was in the EU).
explanation.definitionFit: Goods sold secretly and illegally are traded this way, out of sight of the shop's customers.

clue.text: Hard wood used for steering wheel

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
elm is a wood

explanation.surface: Hardwood was once used for making a ship's wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship is steered from the tiller or wheel, the position known by this nautical word.

clue.text: Parking hold up in operation over not being paid

parts.note: to hold up is to rob at gunpoint
on means working, in operation
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A car-park robbery during an operation, with the victim left unpaid.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for 'for the good', used of professional work given free of charge.

clue.text: General advisor for emperor penguins initially on hold in Antarctica's fringes

indicators.note: the other pieces go inside the outer letters
the fringes of a word are its outermost letters, first and last
in an across clue one piece 'on' another comes after it

parts.note: a grip is a hold

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word penguins

explanation.surface: Emperor penguins huddle on the ice at the edge of Antarctica.
explanation.walkthrough: 'emperor penguins' reads as one species, but 'emperor' belongs to the definition: Marcus Agrippa was the general and right-hand man of the emperor Augustus.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcus Agrippa was Augustus's leading general, admiral and closest counsellor in Rome.

clue.text: Traits distorting economy's top performer

indicators.note: distorting twists the letters of traits out of shape
top points to the first letter of economy's

explanation.surface: Character traits that warp the economy's leading performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional entertainer, especially a singer or dancer, is a stage performer.

clue.text: Satellite of Saturn partly seen overhead

indicators.note: only part of the word overhead is visible, the answer sitting within it

explanation.surface: A moon of Saturn glimpsed in the sky above.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturn's second-largest moon bears the name of the Titan mother of Zeus.

clue.text: Pressure Time to cover Japan's wartime leader, not available to catalogue for snappy reporter?

indicators.note: to here means added at the end, as a further piece joined on

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure

indicators.note: the hour covers the leader's name, which sits inside it

parts.note: an hour is a time
Hideki Tojo was Japan's prime minister during the Second World War
a list is a catalogue

explanation.surface: A journalist pressed for time over Tojo is unavailable to list sources.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snappy' hints at the camera: a reporter who snaps pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: A news photographer tells stories with pictures, a reporter whose work is snapping images.

clue.text: Ailed, suffering with brief bug that one can catch

indicators.note: suffering signals the letters are in a bad way, scrambled
brief means the word is cut short, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: A sick person ailing with a short-lived bug that is catching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catch' looks like catching an infection; it means hear.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound loud enough to be heard is one that the ear can catch, a synonym for hearable.

clue.text: Unexciting wordplay to have?

definitions.meaning: bland, safely moderate and never extreme
in cryptic wordplay 'have' tells you one piece holds another, so the held piece sits in the centre, as if placed down the centre of a street

explanation.surface: A dull remark about what wordplay must contain.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is whimsical: a container indicator like 'have' puts a piece in the middle, the setter's joke being that this is where wordplay wants it.
explanation.definitionFit: A moderate, safe, cautious position avoids extremes, so it is bland and unadventurous.

clue.text: Hood's state when front half's gone wonky

indicators.note: the first half of the word, four of its eight letters, is taken away

parts.note: Robin Hood lived in outlawry, the condition of being an outlaw

explanation.surface: A hood worn askew after its front has been lost.
explanation.walkthrough: Hood is Robin Hood, the outlaw; his state is OUTLAWRY, and losing its front half, OUTL, leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something askew, crooked or out of true: a direct synonym.

clue.text: Tongue and snout getting right inside

indicators.note: the abbreviation for right is placed inside the word for snout

parts.note: a snout is a nose

explanation.surface: An animal's tongue and snout, with something tucked in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tongue' means language here, not the organ beside the snout.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Norse was the language of the Vikings, and tongue is a standard synonym for language.

clue.text: Anna moved on consistently to make an error

wordplay.reading: ANNA with every letter moved one place on in the alphabet

parts.note: move each letter of the name Anna one step forward in the alphabet: A becomes B and N becomes O

explanation.surface: Anna kept moving on and slipped up along the way.
explanation.walkthrough: Shifting every letter of ANNA one place along the alphabet gives a new palindrome.
explanation.definitionFit: A blunder is colloquially called this, and as a verb it means to blunder, slip up.

clue.text: Force away with others

parts.note: the rest means the others

explanation.surface: Pushing something aside along with everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull or wrench something from someone's grip is to force it from them.

clue.text: Fungus just the same with arsenic injected

indicators.note: the chemical symbol is put inside the word, as if injected into it

parts.note: yet means nevertheless, just the same
As is the chemical symbol for arsenic

explanation.surface: A fungus is unchanged despite being injected with poison.
explanation.definitionFit: A single-celled fungus used in brewing and baking, so a type of fungal organism.

clue.text: Eg acquiring this lively piece shows overlap of Dutch artist and German director

indicators.note: Eg takes in the answer, so the merged names are Eg with the answer inside; removing Eg leaves it
the two names overlap, sharing their common letters HER once rather than twice

parts.note: M. C. Escher was the Dutch graphic artist
Werner Herzog is the German film director
taken as written, the two letters E and G

explanation.surface: An art-and-film exhibit merging a Dutch artist and German director.
explanation.walkthrough: ESCHER and HERZOG overlapping on HER make ESCHERZOG; that is E-G 'acquiring this' (the answer), so take away the outer E and G.
explanation.definitionFit: A scherzo is a quick, playful movement in a symphony or sonata, literally a 'joke' in Italian.

clue.text: Podcast's certainly complete in a site for threading

indicators.note: a podcast is heard, not read, so the words are taken as they would be spoken

parts.note: aye means certainly and whole means complete

explanation.surface: A podcaster insists their show is definitely complete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Podcast' is the sound signal: 'aye' sounds like the first part and 'whole' like the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A small hole through which a thread, cord or lace is passed, such as in a needle or shoe.

clue.text: Perhaps used hindsight and reinforced cutter

definitions.meaning: looking back on events, one saw back, read as the answer split in two
a fine-toothed hand saw stiffened along its back edge by a metal strip

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the answer into two words: having 'saw back' is a jokey way to say used hindsight.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenon saw with a strengthening rib along its top is the woodworker's term for this tool.

clue.text: Carriage to have circular form?

definitions.meaning: deportment, the way one carries oneself
split as three words: to be shaped like a circle

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer: to 'be a ring' is to have circular form. 'Carriage' suggests a coach; it means posture.
explanation.definitionFit: Deportment, the way one holds and carries oneself, is a person's posture or mien.

clue.text: Termite trouble mounting through habitual practice

indicators.note: the reversed word runs through the middle of the word for habit

parts.note: wont is habit, customary practice

indicators.note: in a down clue mounting means rising, so the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: ado is fuss, trouble

explanation.surface: Termites cause trouble rising through their routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounting' reverses ADO to ODA, which goes 'through' WONT. A termite is loosely an insect that eats wood, as is this ant.
explanation.definitionFit: Termites are often called white ants, and like this forest ant are wood-dwelling insects: a loose example.

clue.text: Cover with spread set out during tea

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come in the middle of the word for tea, as if during it

parts.note: a brew is a cup of tea

indicators.note: out signals the letters of set are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: Putting out a spread while the tea is brewing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SET into STE, which goes inside BREW ('during').
explanation.definitionFit: To strew things over a surface is to cover it by scattering them about.

clue.text: Black iodine stain on hot metal

parts.note: B is the pencil abbreviation for black
I is the chemical symbol for iodine
smut is a sooty stain
H stands for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A black iodine stain left on a hot piece of metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Element 83 is a brittle, pinkish-white heavy metal used in alloys and medicines.

clue.text: Long twisted inside, twisted by mistake

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go inside the word for twisted

parts.note: wry means twisted, contorted

indicators.note: twisted means the letters of long are turned about

explanation.surface: Something long, twisted inside and out by error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisted' does two jobs: first it rearranges LONG into ONGL, then it gives WRY, which holds those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Done in error or incorrectly, so an adverb meaning mistakenly.

clue.text: A short wharf which supports boats?

indicators.note: short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a quay is a wharf

explanation.surface: A little wharf where boats are moored.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: the thing that holds boats up is water, Latin aqua, not the jetty the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Boats float on water, and this is the Latin word for water used in English.

clue.text: Consequently employment shows a dip

parts.note: so means consequently, therefore
use is employment, as in the employment of a tool

explanation.surface: An economic report: hence the employment figures show a fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a dip' looks like a downturn in jobs, but means a plunge into water.
explanation.definitionFit: A drenching or plunging in liquid; the noun also means a soaking or ducking.

clue.text: Keep talking about old floor

indicators.note: about turns the word for chatter around

parts.note: to yak is to keep talking, chatter on

explanation.surface: Someone keeps chattering about an old floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'floor' is a verb: to knock down, as a boxer is floored by a knockout.
explanation.definitionFit: A phonetic spelling of KO, a boxing knockout; as a verb it means knock someone down.

clue.text: Desire meat sandwich with crusts cut off

indicators.note: removing the crusts takes away the outer letters at each end

parts.note: a burger is a meat patty in a bun

explanation.surface: Craving a meat sandwich with the crusts trimmed off.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong want or impulse, an itch to do something, is a synonym of desire.

clue.text: Against replacing double force of Mediterranean port's coffee

indicators.note: the letter for against takes the place of the two force letters

parts.note: Jaffa is an ancient port on Israel's Mediterranean coast

indicators.note: double asks for the letter for force twice over, two Fs side by side

parts.note: F is the physics symbol for force
V abbreviates versus, against

explanation.surface: Coffee from a Mediterranean port, set against its rival.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang term for coffee, from the Indonesian island where it was famously grown.

clue.text: What might Carl Jung initiate become without one butting in?

indicators.note: the clue's letters rearranged become the answer once the letter for one is taken out of them

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A riddle about what the psychologist Carl Jung might start.
explanation.walkthrough: The sixteen letters of CARL JUNG INITIATE are the answer plus an extra I; 'become without one' rearranges them after removing it.
explanation.definitionFit: To interjaculate is an old word for interjecting, throwing remarks into a conversation.

clue.text: Something put on as play with run in National Theatre

indicators.note: the abbreviation for run goes inside the word for play

parts.note: a game is play
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
NT abbreviates the National Theatre in London

explanation.surface: A production put on as a play at the National Theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' suggests staging a show; it means donning clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing is what you put on your body, so any item of dress is something worn.

clue.text: Cry for attention includes keys to get help? Good for you!

indicators.note: the shout takes the keystrokes inside it

parts.note: hey is a shout to get someone's attention
pressing the Alt key and the H key opens the Help menu in many Windows programs

explanation.surface: Someone shouting for attention while hitting keys to get help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good for you!' looks like praise but is the definition of wholesome.
explanation.definitionFit: Something beneficial to one's health, like a healthy diet, is literally good for you.
